title: Stalemate: no move, but no check
outcomes: Says stalemate when the side to move has no legal move and is not in check
Notices before moving when a move would stalemate the enemy king

steps.text:
**Stalemate:** the player to move is **not** in check and has **no legal move** with any piece. The game ends at once as a **draw**: nobody wins.
One question tells it from checkmate: is the king attacked right now? Yes means checkmate, no means stalemate. A king may never step onto a square an enemy piece attacks, so a king can be stuck even when its neighbouring squares are empty.

steps.text: **Both things must be true.** A boxed-in king is not stalemated if any other piece of its side can still move, even a lone pawn. A pawn blocked by an enemy pawn directly in front has no push, and it can still move if it can capture something diagonally. Here it has neither. Stalemates often happen when one side is far ahead and moves quickly, so count the king's squares, and the other pieces' moves, before a quiet move.

steps.text: **Model answer, to compare with yours.** Stalemate is when the player to move is not in check but has no legal move with any piece; it is a draw. It differs from checkmate by one question: is the king attacked? Before a quiet move near the enemy king, count its moves, and count its other pieces too.
